questions.q: Do you enjoy helping other people?
questions.answer: I really do. My whole job is essentially about helping people reach their goals, and I find that deeply [[fulfilling]]. Even small acts of help brighten my day, and they usually come back around in some form.

questions.q: How do you usually help people in your family?
questions.answer: Mostly with practical things. I sort out bills and online forms for my parents, and I help my younger sister with her English. It's nothing [[heroic]], but it takes a bit of pressure off everyone.

questions.q: Did your parents teach you to help others?
questions.answer: Very much so. My father often let struggling customers pay later, and my mother always shares food with the neighbours. Growing up around that kind of [[generosity]], helping others just became second nature to me.

questions.q: Do people in your country often help their neighbours?
questions.answer: Traditionally, yes, especially in villages and small towns like mine. If someone's ill or there's a wedding, neighbours [[rally round]] without being asked. In big cities like Dhaka, though, people tend to keep themselves to themselves more.

questions.q: Do you think people are less helpful than they used to be?
questions.answer: Not less helpful, just busier. When there's a flood, I've seen people raise money and deliver supplies remarkably quickly, often [[mobilising]] through social media. The kindness is still there, it simply looks different now.
